43583-the-mystery-of-the-fires.title: The Mystery Of The Fires
43583-the-mystery-of-the-fires.creator: Edith Lavell
43583-the-mystery-of-the-fires.description: A book by Edith Lavell. _Residents of Shady Nook_   Reeds two adults and five young people. Hunters mother and son. Partridges four adults. Flick owners of the inn. Robinsons two adults and two boys. Smiths two adults and three children. Ditmar a young married couple. Adams a farmer with three grown-up children. Frazier owners of the Royal Hotel. Eberhardt a village storekeeper.

arxiv-2211-12154.title: Event Causality Identification with Causal News Corpus - Shared Task 3, CASE 2022
arxiv-2211-12154.creator: Fiona Anting Tan, Hansi Hettiarachchi, Ali Hürriyetoğlu, Tommaso Caselli, Onur Uca, Farhana Ferdousi Liza, Nelleke Oostdijk
arxiv-2211-12154.description: Abstract The Event Causality Identification Shared Task of CASE 2022 involved two subtasks working on the Causal News Corpus. Subtask 1 required participants to predict if a sentence contains a causal relation or not. This is a supervised binary classification task. Subtask 2 required participants to identify the Cause, Effect and Signal spans per causal sentence.

arxiv-2503-10482.title: A Rank-One-Update Method for the Training of Support Vector Machines
arxiv-2503-10482.creator: Florian Jarre, Faculty of Mathematics, Natural Sciences
arxiv-2503-10482.description: Abstract This paper considers convex quadratic programs associated with the training of support vector machines (SVMs). Exploiting the special structure of the SVM problem, a new type of active set method with long cycles and stable rank-one-updates is proposed and tested (CMU: cycling method with updates).

arxiv-2508-02262.title: Long-distance device-independent quantum key distribution with standard optics tools
arxiv-2508-02262.creator: Makoto Ishihara, Anthony Brendan, Wojciech Roga, Ulrik L. Andersen, Masahiro Takeoka
arxiv-2508-02262.description: Abstract Device-independent quantum key distribution (DI-QKD) enables information-theoretically secure key exchange between remote parties without any assumptions on the internal workings of the devices used for its implementation. However, its practical deployment remains severely constrained by the need for loophole-free Bell inequality violations, which are highly susceptible to losses and detection efficiencies.

arxiv-2602-20487.title: Height-Dependent Spectrum Activity Measurements and Modeling: A Case Study with FM Radio Bands Thanks: This research is supported in part by the NSF award CNS-2450593.
arxiv-2602-20487.creator: Sung Joon Maeng, Amir Hossein Fahim Raouf, Ozgur Ozdemir, İsmail Güvenç, Mihail L. Sichitiu
arxiv-2602-20487.description: Abstract The increasing demand for wireless connectivity necessitates advanced spectrum modeling to enable efficient spectrum sharing for next-generation aerial communications. While traditional models often overlook vertical variations in signal behavior, this paper proposes a height-dependent propagation model using a helikite-mounted software-defined radio (SDR).

Also, differences in the clinical manifestation and the course of PD have been observed between males and females. However, little is known about the molec

pmc-10537017.title: Eco-Friendly Dispersant-Free Purification Method of Boron Nitride Nanotubes through Controlling Surface Tension and Steric Repulsion with Solvents
pmc-10537017.creator: Minsung Kang, Jungmo Kim, Hongjin Lim, Jaehyoung Ko, Hong-Sik Kim, Yongho Joo, Se Youn Moon, Se Gyu Jang, Eunji Lee, Seokhoon Ahn
pmc-10537017.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs) were purified without the use of a dispersant by controlling the surface tension and steric repulsion of solvent molecules. This method effectively enhanced the difference in solubilities of impurities and BNNTs. The purification process involved optimizing the alkyl-chains of alcohol solvents and adjusting the concentration of alcohol solvent in water to regulate surface tension and steric repulsion.

pmc-10586259.title: Facile Synthesis of gC3N4-Exfoliated BiFeO3 Nanocomposite: A Versatile and Efficient S-Scheme Photocatalyst for the Degradation of Various Textile Dyes and Antibiotics in Water
pmc-10586259.creator: Darshana
pmc-10586259.description: Water pollution engendered from textile dyes and antibiotics is a globally identified precarious concern that is causing dreadful risks to human health as well as aquatic lives. This predicament is escalating the quest to develop competent photocatalysts that can degrade these water pollutants under solar light irradiation.

pmc-12407055.title: HSF2 drives breast cancer progression by acting as a stage-specific switch between proliferation and invasion
pmc-12407055.creator: Jenny C. Pessa, Oona Paavolainen, Hendrik S. E. Hästbacka, Mikael C. Puustinen, Alejandro J. Da Silva, Sandra Pihlström, Silvia Gramolelli, Pia Boström, Pauliina Hartiala, Emilia Peuhu, Jenny Joutsen, Lea Sistonen
pmc-12407055.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Breast cancer is hallmarked by phenotypic transitions enabling abnormal cell proliferation and invasion. The stress-protective transcription factor heat shock factor 2 (HSF2) is associated with cancer, but its function in breast carcinogenesis remains poorly understood. Analysis of human breast tumor samples and mouse in vivo xenografts uncovered that HSF2 expression and activity undergo dynamic changes as a function of tumor progression.

pmc-12468100.title: Collision Tumor of Angioimmunoblastic T-Cell Lymphoma and Kaposi Sarcoma in an HIV-Negative Elderly Woman: The First Reported Case in Asia
pmc-12468100.creator: Myung-Won Lee, Jin-Man Kim
pmc-12468100.description: Background/Objectives: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma (AITL) is a rare peripheral T-cell lymphoma of follicular helper T-cell (TFH) origin, often associated with immune dysregulation and EBV-positive B-cell proliferation. Kaposi sarcoma (KS) is a vascular neoplasm caused by human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8), typically arising in immunocompromised individuals.

pmc-12618523.title: Revealing new associations between lncRNAs and diseases through cross attention mechanism and multiple level feature fusion
pmc-12618523.creator: Xueming Luo, Xiaoling Li, Zongzheng Bai, Yan Jiang
pmc-12618523.description: Revealing new lncRNA-disease associations (LDAs) is necessary to decipher pathological mechanisms and find new clues of diagnosis and therapy for complex diseases. However, experimental methods for LDA identification need a significant amount of time and cost. Here, we introduce a novel deep learning-based method, LDA-CAMF, to infer LDA candidates.

pmc-12619551.title: Individual Autonomic Profiles Influence Brain–Heart Connectivity in Tonic Pain
pmc-12619551.creator: Jana Luisa Aulenkamp, Rasmus B Nedergaard, Imran Khan Niazi, Donghua Liao, Louise Kuhlmann, Fredy Rojas, Kamran Rasool, Anna Evans Phillips, Dhiraj Yadav, Enrique De-Madaria, Peter Hegyi, Pramod Garg, Søren Schou Olesen, Soumya Jagannath, Rasmus Hagn-Meincke, Zoltán Hajnády, Christina Brock, Asbjørn
pmc-12619551.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionAcute pain elicits distinct autonomic responses. Electroencephalography (EEG) and heart rate variability (HRV) provide insights into autonomic and cortical activity to pain, but they often fail to capture the integrated dynamics of brain–heart connectivity.

pmc-12639290.title: Electrocardiographic Profiles by sex in a cohort of healthy Vietnamese university students
pmc-12639290.creator: Thang Nguyen Ngoc, Le Nguyen Thi Nhat, An Pham Van, Soan Hoang Thu, Nghia Nguyen Minh, Thang Vu Tien, Hong Le Thi Bich, Hung Tran Viet, Huyen Pham Thi Thu, Nhung Do Phuong, Linh Tran Thi Thuy, Le Dao Phuong, Cuong Duong Cao, Long Nguyen, Ngoc Nguyen Minh, Chi Do Thi Kim, Hien Nguyen Thu, Huyen Nguye
pmc-12639290.description: Study objectiveTo establish sex-specific electrocardiographic (ECG) reference values in healthy Vietnamese late adolescents and characterize sex-based differences in repolarization patterns.DesignCross-sectional observational study.SettingUniversity health screening program in Vietnam.ParticipantsA total of 5127 first-year university students (58.6 % female; age 17–29 years), all asymptomatic and without known cardiovascular or metabolic disease.InterventionsNone.

pmc-12849185.title: Cohort profile: the Lebanon Study on Aging and HeAlth (LSAHA)
pmc-12849185.creator: Carlos F. Mendes de Leon, Martine Elbejjani, Sawsan Abdulrahim, Hala Ghattas, Aya El Sammak, Alexandra Abi Nassif, Frederic Conrad, Raphael Nishimura, Stephen J. McCall, Abla M. Sibai, Monique Chaaya
pmc-12849185.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThis paper describes the design and cohort profile of the Lebanon Study on Aging and HeAlth (LSAHA), the first population-level study of Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) in an Arab country. The burden due to ADRD in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region is among the highest in the world, but reliable population-level data on ADRD in the region are lacking.

pmc-12965184.title: Metabolomic Differentiation of Malpighiaceae From Dry and Humid Tropics via UHPLC‐MS/MS and Chemometrics
pmc-12965184.creator: Jaqueline Munise Guimarães da Silva, Rafael Felipe de Almeida, Maria Luiza Zeraik
pmc-12965184.description: Various factors can trigger water stress in plants, particularly in those growing in dry tropical regions. To survive under such conditions, plants produce metabolites with adaptive functions. However, metabolomic data on the leaves of Malpighiaceae species cultivated in both dry and humid tropical areas of Brazil remain scarce.

pmc-13025498.title: The Wild Plants from the Family Asteraceae That Are Traditionally Used for Food in Sicily and Bulgaria and Their Health Benefits
pmc-13025498.creator: Ekaterina Kozuharova, Giuseppe Antonio Malfa, Rosaria Acquaviva, Vivienne Spadaro, Iliana Ionkova, Giancarlo Statti, Francesco M. Raimondo
pmc-13025498.description: This study examines 36 wild Asteraceae species that are traditionally used as food in Sicily and Bulgaria, highlighting their ethnobotanical, nutritional, and pharmacological relevance. Some taxa, such as Cichorium intybus, Silybum marianum, Artemisia vulgaris, Taraxacum officinale, and Tussilago farfara, are integral to the Mediterranean and Balkan diets, enhancing nutrition through their fiber, minerals, and bioactive compounds.

pmc-13094780.title: Mislabeling of Case-Control Studies in Ophthalmologic Literature: A Bibliometric Analysis
pmc-13094780.creator: Ting Zeng, Ziping Yu, Jinming Guo, Hongzi Shen, Gehan Ai, Xin Tan, Pi Guo, Kunliang Qiu, Jianwei Lin, Yang Zhuang, Chi-Pui Pang, Hongxi Wang
pmc-13094780.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeTo characterize the prevalence and determinants of case-control study mislabeling in recent ophthalmologic journals.MethodsA bibliometric analysis was conducted on 386 articles self-declared as case-control or case-controlled studies, published from 2022 to 2023 across 95 PubMed-indexed ophthalmologic journals. Two blinded reviewers independently classified study designs using established epidemiological criteria and standardized the Level of Evidence per the Joanna Briggs Institute (2014) guidelines.

pmc-13506335.title: The effect of cohesin mutations on HLA-class II expression in the myeloid leukemia of Down syndrome
pmc-13506335.creator: Austin C Boucher, Wojciech Rosikiewicz, Anitria Cotton, Amber L Broadhurst, Te Ling, Rishika Vadlamudi, Melanie Bremm, Anna-Lena Schmell, Lahiri Konada, Madeline Niederkorn, Josiah D Murray, Yichao Li, Shilpa Narina, Sarah Inglott, Anindita Roy, Philip Ancliff, Ricky Tirtakusuma, Jing Ma, Michael P
pmc-13506335.description: Children with Down syndrome (DS) frequently develop transient abnormal myelopoiesis that can evolve to the myeloid leukemia of DS (ML-DS). TAM spontaneously resolves in most cases but progresses to ML-DS with additional mutations, most commonly in the cohesin complex. However, the mechanisms by which these alterations promote leukemia are unknown.

pmc-13587545.title: Shared oral microbiome signatures linking periodontitis and autoimmune thyroiditis: NHANES 2009–2012
pmc-13587545.creator: Xiangkun Meng, Lei Li, Rui Hao, Zhifeng Lin, Ke Liu, Gaoman Chi, Jingyuan Ren, Ru Liu, Yuge Gao, Xiaotong Yu, Xiaolin Tong
pmc-13587545.description: ObjectiveTo examine the association between periodontitis severity and autoimmune thyroiditis (AIT) in a nationally representative US sample and to explore oral microbiome features shared between the two conditions.MethodsWe analyzed adults from NHANES 2009–2012 with complete periodontal examinations, thyroid autoantibodies, and oral microbiome data (n = 1,346). Periodontitis was classified using CDC/AAP case definitions.

pmc-13681528.creator: Zixu Wang, Simon Reinke, Yu Shen, Xiangyi Deng, Tobias Alexander, Anne Claußnitzer, Sebastian Hardt, Luis Becker, Koji Tokoyoda, Carsten Perka, Andreas Radbruch, Jun Dong
